one_month_reasoning: One big scheduled event in the window: Q3 2026 results and Q4 guidance on Oct 15, 2026 (quiet period Oct 5-14) [17]. Q3 should beat: July+August revenue is running at the top of the US$44.6-45.8B guide (August NT$514.8B, +53% YoY) [2], the NT$ is ~31.6-31.8 against a 32 guidance assumption, and UBS expects revenue and GM at the high end [8]. The skeptic point is that a beat is priced in. In July a record quarter and a raised guide still saw the ADR fall ~4% on margin guidance and capex [3], and the stock has already rallied to near its 52-week high. The swing factors on the call are Q4 GM (2nm dilution of 3-4pt [18], equipment inflation [8]) and early 2027 capex or growth color. Also in the window: the September revenue release (~Oct 9) and the macro/AI tape. Taiwan-strait or Section 232 headlines are possible but not scheduled. I set the median a touch above spot (~$461) and a log-sd of ~12%, slightly above the 11.4% normal monthly vol (40%/3.5) to reflect the earnings event. That is roughly symmetric: no strong directional call.

fair_value.method: 70% P/E: Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$22.7/ADR (consensus FY27 $21.93 and FY28 rolled at +12%, haircut 5%) x 18x = $409. 30% FCF yield: FY27 FCF ~$10.1/ADR at a 2.75% yield = $369. Blended fair value about $397, ~14% below spot.

methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 = 0.25*FY27 $21.93 + 0.75*FY28 $24.56 = $23.90; less 5% skeptic haircut = $22.7; x 18x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Vantage average of 13 analysts. It was revised up from $19.66 90 days ago.
FY27 consensus x 1.12. Goldman sees hyperscaler AI capex growth slowing to ~12% in 2028, and foundry revenue growth is assumed to track it.
Covers 2nm/overseas GM dilution of 3-4pt [18], equipment price inflation [8], low-quality Q2 profit growth flattered by the ~$2B Vanguard gain [3], and depreciation-wall demand risk in 2027-28 [7].

Today's ~22x forward ($459 / ~$20.7 NTM from [4]) sits on peak margins (GM 67.7% [1]). With capex growth decelerating [20], I expect compression toward the high-teens mid-cycle level that the bear write-ups use [16].

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY27 revenue ~$230B x 62% OCF margin - $90B capex = ~$52.6B FCF / 5.19B ADR-equivalents = $10.1/ADR; / 2.75% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Vantage revenue consensus of NT$7.32T converted at the ~31.8 spot rate. UBS is higher at $240.7B [8].

Q2 net margin was 55.6% [1]; D&A adds to that, and working capital and taxes take some back. Q2 OCF less capex came to $9.09B FCF after quarterly capex of ~$15B [3]. I set the margin a little below the implied ~64% to allow for prepayments to equipment suppliers [8].
UBS forecast of $90B [8], up from the 2026 guide of $60-64B [18].
Q2 net income (55.6% x $40.20B = $22.35B) / EPS of $4.31 per ADR.

An AA-/Aa3 credit [9] with USD bond spreads of ~110-120bp [10] gives a ~4.5% cost of debt. A 2.75% FCF yield implies ~4-5% long-run FCF growth on an ~7.5% equity cost, which is reasonable for a capex-heavy monopolist mid-cycle.

bear.story: A 2027 AI digestion: hyperscaler D&A crosses over and capex growth slows sharply [7,20], Nvidia (>20% of revenue [14]) cuts orders, and 2nm/Arizona dilution plus equipment inflation hit GM. FY28 EPS flattens near ~$20 and the multiple de-rates to ~14x. A non-invasion Taiwan or tariff shock (e.g., a Section 232 chip list [11]) would also land here.

base.story: EPS grows ~25-30% into 2027 as consensus expects [4], but the multiple compresses from ~22x to ~19-20x as growth decelerates and capex intensity rises. The stock ends roughly flat to slightly up.

bull.story: AI demand keeps surprising (UBS-style 40% 2027 growth to $240B at ~67% GM [8]), 2028 EPS reaches ~$27, and the stock holds ~24x on pricing power and N2/A16 monopoly status.

thesis_break_reason: $330 is ~28% below spot and ~16x consensus FY27 EPS. A move there would very likely mean the 2027 earnings path is being cut, through an AI order pause or Nvidia/hyperscaler capex cuts or a structural GM reset below ~58%, or that a geopolitical or tariff discount is being priced in. Normal 40%-vol multiple noise would not usually get it that far.

reasoning: Fundamentals are excellent, and the skeptic has to admit it. Q2 GM was 67.7% [1], FY26 growth was raised to slightly above 40% [18], August revenue was +53% YoY [2], FY27 EPS consensus has risen ~12% in 90 days [4], and the credit is AA-/Aa3 with a positive outlook [9]. I found no accounting, credit, insider or litigation red flags of size: insider sales are small [13], and the 2nm leak case went in TSMC's favor [12]. The real bear case is (1) a valuation that rests on peak margins and on growth that is ~100% AI (HPC was 108% of Q2 sequential growth, and Q2 net income growth was flattered by the Vanguard sale [3]); (2) a 2027-28 demand air-pocket as hyperscaler depreciation compounds [7] and capex growth slows to ~12% in 2028 [20], with capital-destruction warnings from strategists [19] and heavy Nvidia exposure [14]; (3) rising capital intensity, with capex at $60-64B in 2026 and ~$90B expected in 2027 plus supplier inflation [8]; and (4) geopolitical and tariff tails. Polymarket prices a 9% chance of invasion by Jun-2027 ($462k volume) and 13% by Dec-2027 ($3.3M) [5,6], and the Section 232 chip list is still pending [11]. My fair value of ~$397 sits below spot, but momentum and upward revisions are strong, so the 12-month median is ~$455 (about flat): EPS growth offsets multiple compression. The ladder mixes a 96%-weight lognormal (median $455, sigma 0.38, near the 40% realized vol) with a 4% crash state (median $160) for a cross-strait or blockade shock. I deliberately put the crash weight below Polymarket's raw odds, because 'invasion' markets tend to overstate and a gray-zone blockade could have a different price impact. Scenario mean is ~$458.
